text:
miriam (product): quick sync — we need to finalize the customer-managed networking contract language and the upgrade window guarantees for private deployments. can we align on minimal commitments?
jonathan (eng): +1. customer asks: they want to manage BGP sessions and keep control of IP ranges during upgrades.
lee (netops): absolutely possible but needs clear rollback/runbook guarantees. we should define a 30m maintenance window for control-plane upgrades, and an opt-in extended window for full infra churn.
sarah (solutions): customers will push back on any forced IP reassignments. propose we promise 'no IP renumbering' during rolling upgrades as default. exceptions documented.
devon (sre): we need an SLA for upgrade-induced outage: SLO = 99.9% control plane up outside maintenance windows. during a declared window, we allow up to 5m of brief traffic steering.
miriam (product): ok. draft proposal: 1) customer maintains BGP and IPs; 2) we own runtime binary upgrades; 3) default rolling upgrade with zero IP renumbering; 4) standard maintenance window 30m; opt-in extended up to 4h for major schema/network changes. any blockers?
jonathan (eng): technical note — some quantized model artifacts require short cache flushes that can briefly spike egress while the KV caches rebuild. we can avoid IP changes but expect short path reconvergence. document this as expected behaviour.
lee (netops): add a pre-upgrade validation step that runs in the customer's network namespace. visible via a webhook + dry-run report. customers can opt to fail the rollout if validation fails.
sarah (solutions): need a clear UX in the console: "preflight checks", a pass/fail report, and an explicit toggle for "allow extended window". also capture contact for on-call.
devon (sre): fallback policy: if network preflight fails, auto-abort and open a rollback with a single click. add a staggered canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 10m observation intervals.
miriam (product): good. i want short, customer-facing bullets for the legal contract as well: "we do not change customer IPs; we will coordinate maintenance windows; we provide preflight checks and rollback; urgent security patches may be applied with 24h notice unless customer opts into emergency SLA."
jonathan (eng): can we include a short snippet for ops docs showing the preflight curl?
lee (netops): sure, here's a sample preflight call customers can run to validate peerings:
```
curl -X POST https://private.redwood.example/preflight \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -d '{"bgp_peer": "10.0.0.1", "prefixes": ["10.0.0.0/24"]}'
```
miriam (product): perfect. put that in the field guide. who owns the rollout playbook writeup?
sarah (solutions): i'll own the customer-facing playbook and template emails for scheduling. jonathan + devon own the technical runbook and canary scripts. lee will supply the network validation checklist.
devon (sre): i'll add the canary tooling to the deploy pipeline and wire the webhook -> incident creation on failure. deploy-bot will post progress.
deploy-bot: scheduled rollout created: private-deploy/vpc-upgrade/1768429012. canary steps: 10% -> 50% -> 100%. watch channel: #release-war-room.
lee (netops): one open question — do we allow customers to self-trigger an immediate rollback? extra risk but improves trust. recommend we allow self-rollback within the first 20 minutes after a canary step.
jonathan (eng): implementation detail: self-rollback must quiesce new tokens and invalidate KV cache snapshots created post-canary. otherwise we risk divergence. add that to docs.
miriam (product): decision: allow self-rollback within 20m of a canary step. document token quiesce and cache invalidation as necessary steps.
sarah (solutions): I'll draft the scheduling UI text and sample contract bullets. goal: publish to docs and notify field by EOD Wed.
miriam (product): thanks all. followups: jonathan — add expected cache-rebuild timeline to the tech runbook (est 2-8m). devon — add deploy-bot hooks for preflight result and canary metrics. lee — provide a minimal network checklist and example BGP configs. i'll update contract language and share with legal.
jonathan (eng): noted. pushing a PR to the runbook repo shortly.
lee (netops): will send checklist and BGP examples by EOD.
devon (sre): will wire deploy-bot tests and stub webhook receiver today.
miriam (product): closing the thread — thanks. tagging @sarah (solutions) to remind for the field announcement. :thumbsup:
